L24: # WTSQueryUserToken function (wtsapi32.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: ## In this article
L30: 
L31: Obtains the primary access token of the logged-on user specified by the session ID. To call this function successfully, the calling application must be running within the context of the 【5†LocalSystem account】 and have the SE_TCB_NAME privilege.
L32: Caution  WTSQueryUserToken is intended for highly trusted services. Service providers must use caution that they do not leak user tokens when calling this function. Service providers must close token handles after they have finished using them.
L33: ## Syntax
L34: 
L35:     `BOOL WTSQueryUserToken(
L36:       [in]  ULONG   SessionId,
L37:       [out] PHANDLE phToken
L38:     );
L39:     `
L40: ## Parameters
L41: 
L42: `[in] SessionId`
L43: 
L44: A Remote Desktop Services session identifier. Any program running in the context of a service will have a session identifier of zero (0). You can use the 【6†WTSEnumerateSessions】 function to retrieve the identifiers of all sessions on a specified RD Session Host server.
L45: To be able to query information for another user's session, you need to have the Query Information permission. For more information, see 【7†Remote Desktop Services Permissions】. To modify permissions on a session, use the Remote Desktop Services Configuration administrative tool.
L46: 
L47: `[out] phToken`
L48: 
L49: If the function succeeds, receives a pointer to the token handle for the logged-on user. Note that you must call the 【8†CloseHandle】 function to close this handle.
L50: ## Return value
L51: 
L52: If the function succeeds, the return value is a nonzero value, and the phToken parameter points to the primary token of the user.
L53: 
L54: If the function fails, the return value is zero. To get extended error information, call 【9†GetLastError】.
L55: ## Remarks
L56: 
L57: For information about primary tokens, see 【10†Access Tokens】. For more information about account privileges, see 【7†Remote Desktop Services Permissions】 and 【11†Authorization Constants】.
L58: 
L59: See 【5†LocalSystem account】 for information about the privileges associated with that account.
L60: ## Requirements
L61: 
L62: Requirement  | Value
L63: --- | ---
L64: Minimum supported client  | Windows Vista
L65: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server 2008
L66: Target Platform  | Windows

L68: Library  | Wtsapi32.lib
L69: DLL  | Wtsapi32.dll
L70: API set  | ext-ms-win-session-wtsapi32-l1-1-0 (introduced in Windows 8)

L24: # OpenProcessToken function (processthreadsapi.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The OpenProcessToken function opens the 【5†access token】 associated with a process.
L33: 
L34: ## Syntax
L35: 
L36:     `BOOL OpenProcessToken(
L37:       [in]  HANDLE  ProcessHandle,
L38:       [in]  DWORD   DesiredAccess,
L39:       [out] PHANDLE TokenHandle
L40:     );
L41:     `
L42: ## Parameters
L43: 
L44: `[in] ProcessHandle`
L45: 
L46: A handle to the process whose access token is opened. The process must have the PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION access permission. See 【6†Process Security and Access Rights】 for more info.
L47: 
L48: `[in] DesiredAccess`
L49: 
L50: Specifies an 【5†access mask】 that specifies the requested types of access to the access token. These requested access types are compared with the 【7†discretionary access control list】 (DACL) of the token to determine which accesses are granted or denied.
L51: For a list of access rights for access tokens, see 【8†Access Rights for Access-Token Objects】.
L52: 
L53: `[out] TokenHandle`
L54: 
L55: A pointer to a handle that identifies the newly opened access token when the function returns.
L56: ## Return value
L57: 
L58: If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero.
L59: 
L60: If the function fails, the return value is zero. To get extended error information, call 【9†GetLastError】.
L61: ## Remarks
L62: 
L63: To get a handle to an elevated process from within a non-elevated process, both processes must be started from the same account.
L64: 
L65: If the process being checked was started by a different account, the checking process needs to have the SE_DEBUG_NAME privilege enabled. See 【10†Privilege Constants (Authorization)】 for more info.
L66: 
L67: To close the access token handle returned through the TokenHandle parameter, call 【11†CloseHandle】.

L69:

L72: Minimum supported client  | Windows XP [desktop apps | UWP apps]
L73: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server 2003 [desktop apps | UWP apps]

L76: Library  | Advapi32.lib

L24: # DuplicateTokenEx function (securitybaseapi.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The DuplicateTokenEx function creates a new 【5†access token】 that duplicates an existing token. This function can create either a 【6†primary token】 or an 【7†impersonation token】.
L33: ## Syntax
L34: 
L35:     `BOOL DuplicateTokenEx(
L36:       [in]           HANDLE                       hExistingToken,
L37:       [in]           DWORD                        dwDesiredAccess,
L38:       [in, optional] LPSECURITY_ATTRIBUTES        lpTokenAttributes,
L39:       [in]           SECURITY_IMPERSONATION_LEVEL ImpersonationLevel,
L40:       [in]           TOKEN_TYPE                   TokenType,
L41:       [out]          PHANDLE                      phNewToken
L42:     );
L43:     `
L44: ## Parameters
L45: 
L46: `[in] hExistingToken`
L47: 
L48: A handle to an access token opened with TOKEN_DUPLICATE access.
L49: 
L50: `[in] dwDesiredAccess`
L51: Specifies the requested access rights for the new token. The DuplicateTokenEx function compares the requested access rights with the existing token's 【8†discretionary access control list】 (DACL) to determine which rights are granted or denied. To request the same access rights as the existing token, specify zero. To request all access rights that are valid for the caller, specify MAXIMUM_ALLOWED.
L52: 
L53: For a list of access rights for access tokens, see 【9†Access Rights for Access-Token Objects】.
L54: `[in, optional] lpTokenAttributes`
L55: 
L56: A pointer to a 【10†SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES】 structure that specifies a 【11†security descriptor】 for the new token and determines whether child processes can inherit the token. If lpTokenAttributes is NULL, the token gets a default security descriptor and the handle cannot be inherited. If the security descriptor contains a 【11†system access control list】 (SACL), the token gets ACCESS_SYSTEM_SECURITY access right, even if it was not requested in dwDesiredAccess.
L57: To set the owner in the security descriptor for the new token, the caller's process token must have the SE_RESTORE_NAME privilege set.
L58: 
L59: `[in] ImpersonationLevel`
L60: 
L61: Specifies a value from the 【12†SECURITY_IMPERSONATION_LEVEL】 enumeration that indicates the impersonation level of the new token.
L62: 
L63: `[in] TokenType`
L64: 
L65: Specifies one of the following values from the 【13†TOKEN_TYPE】 enumeration.
L66: 
L67: Value  | Meaning
L68: --- | ---
L69: TokenPrimary
L70:  | The new token is a 【6†primary token】 that you can use in the 【14†CreateProcessAsUser】 function.
L71: 
L72: TokenImpersonation
L73:  | The new token is an impersonation token.
L74: 
L75: `[out] phNewToken`
L76: 
L77: A pointer to a HANDLE variable that receives the new token.
L78: 
L79: When you have finished using the new token, call the 【15†CloseHandle】 function to close the token handle.
L80: ## Return value
L81: 
L82: If the function succeeds, the function returns a nonzero value.
L83: 
L84: If the function fails, it returns zero. To get extended error information, call 【16†GetLastError】.
L85: ## Remarks
L86: 
L87: The DuplicateTokenEx function allows you to create a 【6†primary token】 that you can use in the 【14†CreateProcessAsUser】 function. This allows a server application that is impersonating a client to create a process that has the 【11†security context】 of the client. Note that the 【17†DuplicateToken】 function can create only impersonation tokens, which are not valid for CreateProcessAsUser.
L88: The following is a typical scenario for using DuplicateTokenEx to create a 【6†primary token】. A server application creates a thread that calls one of the impersonation functions, such as 【18†ImpersonateNamedPipeClient】, to impersonate a client. The impersonating thread then calls the 【19†OpenThreadToken】 function to get its own token, which is an 【7†impersonation token】 that has the security context of the client.
L89: The thread specifies this impersonation token in a call to DuplicateTokenEx, specifying the TokenPrimary flag. The DuplicateTokenEx function creates a primary token that has the security context of the client.
L90: ## Requirements

L95: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server 2003 [desktop apps | UWP apps]

L98: Library  | Advapi32.lib
L99: DLL  | Advapi32.dll
